extracted.intended_audience: students and public-relations/communications professionals writing press releases (e.g., university communications staff, journalists)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing news-style press releases that communicate new, useful information to targeted media and audiences; covers content, structure, style, brevity, audience targeting, distribution, and media-specific formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contain new and useful information
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases should contain new and useful information that readers will want or need to know
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release must present information that is timely and provides value to the intended readership; avoid rehashing stale or irrelevant details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main idea and purpose at the beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: Main idea and purpose should be at the beginning
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with the most important fact or news hook so readers and reporters immediately understand why the release matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise, tight writing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sentence must be meaningful. Cut anything unnecessary or padding; prefer brevity while preserving clarity and necessary context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target audience focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Make target audience interested in information; consider venue of release; account for secondary audience members; but write specifically for primary target
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the primary audience (e.g., trade journalists, general public, funders) and tailor tone, detail, and examples to them while acknowledging potential secondary readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo caution and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious with embargoes - media outlets often don't like holding releases; embargo only when there's clear need
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use embargoes sparingly; unless essential, embargoing can result in outlets refusing to hold content and losing placement in the news cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt format to distribution medium
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust content and presentation to the chosen media (see specific format guidance). Ensure the release reads and functions well in the venue where it will appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format-specific guidance (audio/print/online/broadcast)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio-only: avoid long strings of numbers; Audio: avoid visual references; Black-and-white print: avoid color-dependent descriptions; Color media: can leverage visual descriptions; Online: use multimedia, hyperlinks; Broadcast: use shorter sentences, simpler vocabulary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing for a specific medium, follow these concrete adjustments: remove visual-only references for audio, simplify language for broadcast, avoid color cues for black-and-white, and exploit links/multimedia for online distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply AP style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Associated Press conventions for spelling, capitalization, numbers, datelines, attribution, and other newsroom style points to increase pickup and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use active voice and concrete language
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor active constructions and specific, concrete wording over passive or vague phrasing to make the release clearer and more engaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear paragraph structure and factual tone
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize information into clear paragraphs (lead, context, quotes, boilerplate) and maintain a factual, non-hyperbolic tone suitable for journalistic use.
